fixture_formats.record_digest: SHA-256 over UTF-8 of JCS of the whole object, sig included

cases.description: Envelope C with its artifact octets replaced after signing. artifact_digest FAIL, so anchor_inclusion is never run (§6.2.1 step 4); §8.1 row 2.
A validly signed envelope for request C that binds the digest of another request. request_binding FAIL; §8.1 row 2.

Envelope C naming the trusted responder key, signed by another key. envelope_signature FAIL, so anchor_inclusion is never run (§6.2.1 step 4); §8.1 row 2. responder_trust checks the named key and passes (reading P-54).
Envelope C signed by, and naming, a key the trust policy does not accept. responder_trust FAIL; §8.1 row 2. The material still proves the artifact (§6.2.1 step 4 does not depend on trust).
A request for another record, answered with envelope C's subject. subject_binding FAIL; §8.1 row 2.
A request pinning another checkpoint, answered under §10.1's checkpoint. anchor_match FAIL; §8.1 row 2. The material proves the artifact under the checkpoint the envelope names.
Envelope C with one octet of its inclusion proof changed in transit. verification_binding FAIL, so anchor_inclusion is never run (§6.2.1 step 4); §8.1 row 2 (§10.1, last paragraph).
The changed inclusion proof, with the envelope re-signed over its digest. The material is bound, and does not prove the artifact: anchor_inclusion FAIL at §6.2.1 step 12; §8.1 row 2.
A refusal that verifies under its own key_id, a key the trust policy does not accept. responder_trust FAIL: a response received and failed, UNKNOWN; never a refusal outcome.
A refusal naming the trusted responder key, signed by another key. refusal_signature FAIL; UNKNOWN. responder_trust checks the named key against the policy and passes (reading P-54).

Envelope C signed by a key of small order, the identity point, that the trust policy accepts, with R the identity point and S zero, which a lenient verifier accepts over any message. Strict Ed25519 (§5.2) refuses it: envelope_signature FAIL, so anchor_inclusion is never run (§6.2.1 step 4). responder_trust checks the named key against the policy and passes (reading P-54).

Envelope C signed by the trusted responder's own key with R the identity point, a signature only that key holder can make and that a lenient verifier accepts. Strict Ed25519 (§5.2) refuses it: envelope_signature FAIL, so anchor_inclusion is never run (§6.2.1 step 4).

A refusal signed by a key of small order, the identity point, that the trust policy accepts, with R the identity point and S zero, which a lenient verifier accepts over any message. Strict Ed25519 (§5.2) refuses it: refusal_signature FAIL; UNKNOWN. responder_trust checks the named key against the policy and passes (reading P-54).

A refusal signed by the trusted responder's own key with R the identity point, a signature only that key holder can make and that a lenient verifier accepts. Strict Ed25519 (§5.2) refuses it: refusal_signature FAIL; UNKNOWN.
A conforming refusal with reason policy_declined. WITHHELD, which projects to GAP; the claim's carrier is analysis or story, never disclosure.
A conforming refusal with reason no_such_subject: evidence not found. NOT_FOUND, projecting to GAP.
A conforming refusal with reason capacity_exceeded, registered by ER -02: the responder states a limit of its own. UNKNOWN, never WITHHELD: it says nothing about the evidence or the policy.
A conforming refusal with reason request_unauthenticated, registered by ER -02: the request's authentication did not verify, a property of the request. UNKNOWN.

The same reason answering a request that asks for evidence-interop/0, checked by a verifier that implements both identifiers. evidence-interop/0 pins ER -01, where capacity_exceeded is unregistered: reason_registered FAIL, a response received and failed, UNKNOWN.

A conforming refusal under evidence-interop/2 that carries policy_digest, signed with the three ERV A7 members. Every property PASS; NOT_FOUND. The signature binds the digest of the responder's policy to this refusal.
A conforming refusal under evidence-interop/2 with no policy_digest: the member is optional, and the signing input is the three ERV A7 members. Every property PASS; NOT_FOUND.
The signed refusal with its policy_digest replaced by another digest after signing. refusal_signature FAIL: a response received and failed, UNKNOWN.
The signed refusal with its policy_digest removed after signing. The signing input is then the three ERV A7 members, which the signature does not cover: refusal_signature FAIL; UNKNOWN.

A refusal answering a request for evidence-interop/2, signed over the three ERV A7 members only, with a policy_digest added beside them. Under evidence-interop/2 a policy_digest present is signed: refusal_signature FAIL; UNKNOWN.
A refusal whose signed policy_digest is uppercase hexadecimal, not the §5.2 digest form. The signature verifies, but a signed member is malformed: refusal_signature FAIL; UNKNOWN.

A request for evidence-interop/1 and its ERV A7 refusal, as a responder implementing evidence-interop/1 signs it, checked by a verifier implementing evidence-interop/1 and evidence-interop/2: the refusal is checked under the identifier its request asks for. Every property PASS; NOT_FOUND.

A request for evidence-interop/1 answered by an ERV A7 refusal that carries a policy_digest outside its signature. Under evidence-interop/1 the signing input is the three members whatever else the refusal carries, so every property PASS and NOT_FOUND, and the policy_digest binds nothing: a verifier never reports it as the responder's.

A request for evidence-interop/1 answered by a refusal signed under the evidence-interop/2 rule, its policy_digest inside the signature. Under evidence-interop/1 the signing input is the three ERV A7 members, which the signature does not cover: refusal_signature FAIL; UNKNOWN. A responder answers each request under the identifier it asks for.

A request for evidence-interop/9, which no verifier implements, answered by an ERV A7 refusal that carries a policy_digest outside its signature, checked by a verifier implementing evidence-interop/1 and evidence-interop/2. The signature verifies over the A7 members, the input of evidence-interop/1: refusal_signature PASS, every property PASS and NOT_FOUND. That input excludes policy_digest, so the member binds nothing: a verifier never reports it as the responder's.

A request for evidence-interop/9 answered by a refusal signed with the evidence-interop/2 input over a policy_digest, checked by a verifier implementing evidence-interop/1 and evidence-interop/2. The signature verifies over the input of evidence-interop/2, whose rules the refusal meets: every property PASS; NOT_FOUND.

The same, signed over an uppercase policy_digest. The signature verifies only over the input of evidence-interop/2, which brings its rule that a signed policy_digest is a digest (§5.2): refusal_signature FAIL; UNKNOWN.

The signed refusal of refusal-policy-digest-signed, checked by a verifier that implements evidence-interop/1 only. It does not implement evidence-interop/2, so it checks the signature under the identifiers it does implement, none of which signs policy_digest: refusal_signature FAIL; UNKNOWN. A requester that wants policy_digest signed asks for evidence-interop/2.
Nothing arrived for request C within its one-minute window. The requester's absence record maps to UNKNOWN, never to a refusal; the claim SHOULD use story.

The absence record of missing-evidence-recorded-absence, signed by the requester. The signing input is JCS of every member except sig, key_id included (§6.4). Conforming; the same UNKNOWN as the unsigned record.

The same absence record, signed over every member except key_id and sig: the refusal's signing input (§6.3), not the absence record's (§6.4). The signature does not verify, so the record is not a conforming absence and no claim is made from it.
The same absence record with key_id and no sig. key_id and sig are both present or both absent (§6.4), so the record is not a conforming absence and no claim is made from it.

The same absence record with the valid sig of missing-evidence-recorded-absence-signed and no key_id. key_id and sig are both present or both absent (§6.4), so the record is not a conforming absence and no claim is made from it.

Request C asks for evidence-interop/2; the envelope names evidence-interop/1. The verifier implements both, so only the mismatch rule of §3.3 step 5 applies: profile_version FAIL and every other envelope property NOT_CHECKED; §8.1 row 2.
An artifact response with no profile member, as from a responder implementing the Evidence Request draft alone. profile_version NOT_PRESENT; §8.1 row 3.

A request and envelope under evidence-interop/1, checked by a verifier that implements only evidence-interop/2. profile_version NOT_CHECKED, every other property NOT_CHECKED, never checked under v2 rules; §8.1 row 4.
A request naming evidence-interop/9, which the responder does not implement. It refuses with request_malformed (§3.3 step 4); a conforming refusal, UNKNOWN.

Every envelope property PASS; the carried JWS fails its own signature check. The requirement that IS the check is SATISFIED and not_met (row 5); the one the check only SUPPORTS is INSUFFICIENT (row 6).

cases.description: A proposal and an execution record, and no answer from the acceptor. No candidate: not_accepted, and the requirements are the requester's own expectations.
§11.1.9 A: an acceptance written after the action, dated before it, with no ordering evidence. It must not reach accepted_before_action.
§11.1.9 B: a receipt signed by the acceptor itself does not count as ordering evidence.
§11.1.9 C: an honest receipt from the proposer, received after the action. It counts, and its ordering point is not earlier than the action: INCONCLUSIVE.
§11.1.9 D: an accepted record whose own issued_at is after the action. The acceptor's own record admits it: acceptance_ordering FAIL, accepted_after_action.
§11.1.9 E: the same record bytes as A, with a proposer's receipt received before the action. PASS, accepted_before_action.
§11.1.9 F: the trust policy maps the proposer key to the acceptor's party. Neither key is accepted in its role: not_accepted.
§11.1.9 G: the inputs of E, while the action truly took place at 00:01. The true time is not an input, so the result is E's: the limit of §11.1.10.

§11.1.5 rule 2 at the boundary: the accepted record's issued_at equals the action time at the precision held, as when a producer holds times to the minute. Equal times do not order the two, so rule 2 does not apply; the proposer's receipt at that same time is not earlier: INCONCLUSIVE.
§11.1.5 rule 2 at the boundary: the accepted record's issued_at is one second after the action time: acceptance_ordering FAIL, accepted_after_action.
§11.1.9 G under a trust policy requiring a time for the action from a party other than the acceptor: none is held, so acceptance_ordering is NOT_PRESENT (§11.1.5 rule 3).
§11.2.7 A: N supersedes I's record. lifecycle_not_issuer; no effect.
§11.2.7 B, control: I supersedes its own record.
§11.2.7 C: issuer names I, the signature is N's. lifecycle_signature FAIL; the issuer is not established.
§11.2.7 D: S_N and S_I, in either order. Only S_I qualifies, so it is unique.
§11.2.7 D in the other order of receipt: the same findings and state.
§11.2.7 E: N amends I's record. lifecycle_not_issuer.
§11.2.7 F: I2, mapped to I's party but not a successor, supersedes. lifecycle_not_issuer.
§11.2.7 G: the trust policy states that I2 succeeds I.
§11.2.7 H: N disputes I's record through process p. Effective; one open dispute; content unchanged.
§11.2.7 I: two supersessions of R0 by I. Both forked; no latest supported state.
